chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from Marwan ibn Shuja', from Salim al-Afatas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'im) said: 'Anyone from the Qadariyyah who does not exaggerate [in their view] has exited from faith.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin, title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْإِيمَانِ: Faith, belief in God and the principles of religion
key_terms.الْقَدَرِيَّةِ: Qadariyyah, a theological sect emphasizing human free will and often denying divine decree (al-Qadr)

ai.seo_question: What is the status of the Qadariyyah in Shia theology according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) declares that anyone who separates themselves from the doctrine of Al-Qadar (divine decree) by adopting the extreme Qadariyyah view of absolute human free will has exited the fold of faith. This narration, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, underscores the Shia theological stance that while humans possess agency, it operates within the broader framework of divine will, and denying this balance constitutes a departure from true Iman.
